nodes.label: Patient had a pruritic and painful periorbital eruption lasting 1 month

Patient is a woman in her 70s with a medical history of lupus nephritis requiring hemodialysis, immune thrombocytopenia, acute myeloid leukemia, chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, deep vein thrombosis, diverticulitis, and postcolectomy diarrhea
Past treatments included hydroxychloroquine, which resulted in retinal toxic effects, and lenalidomide, which severely worsened platelet count with a nadir of 28 ×10^3/μL
Physical examination demonstrated scaly, crusted pink plaques involving the periorbital skin
Left upper eyelid biopsy shows vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy
Discoid lupus erythematosus (chronic cutaneous lupus erythematosus)
Biopsy lacks fungal elements or viral cytopathic changes
PAS/culture and HSV/VZV PCR are pending
DIF, ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Ro/La, C3/C4, and drug timeline remain pending/missing
